text:
alex: Heads-up — ran a concurrency sweep on the new 8-bit-small-v2 bring-up overnight. Cost-per-token looks great but p95 latency jumps around 200qps. dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/evals/8bit-small-v2 :eyes:
maya: ugh, did you compare with baseline fp16?
sara: baseline p95 is stable up to ~400qps right?
alex: yeah fp16 stays flat. this variant shows weird tail spikes and occasional 503s from runner.
mason: can you paste the loadgen command and config you used?
alex: loadgen cmd: `./loadgen --model 8bit-small-v2 --qps 200-500 --concurrency 16 --batch_window_ms 8 --duration 30m --kv_cache on`
maya: batch_window 8ms might interact badly with continuous batching + kv cache. try 2ms and no prefetch.
sara: also check runner allocation — the autoscaler might be bouncing instances if p95 crosses 250ms threshold.
alex: log excerpt:

```
runner-23 WARN: batch window expanded to 64ms for 12 requests
runner-23 ERROR: backend 127.0.0.1:9001 fell back with 503
inference: kvcache hit-rate 0.93
```

mason: that batch window expand line is interesting — why did it go to 64ms from 8ms? batching logic shouldn't do that unless backlog is high.
maya: could be backpressure from slower kernel on certain sequence lengths due to int8 microkernels. quant kernels sometimes have stragglers for len > 1024.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0423 — high p95 on 8bit-small-v2 (assigned to eng-ml).
ci-bot: perf-ci job `evals/concurrency/8bit-small-v2` failed on step `p95-regression-check` — diff +82ms vs baseline. link: https://ci.internal/job/9876
sara: quick triage plan: 1) repro with batch_window=2ms and kv_cache off 2) run with forced single-kernel path (fallback to bf16 path) 3) capture runner profiling (gpu_util + kernel timings) 4) sanity-check autoscaler logs for churn
mason: I'll take step 1, run in region-us-west2 with smaller instances to see if it's CPU or kernel bound.
maya: I'll prep a runner build with an env flag to disable int8 fused-ops so we can isolate microkernel variance.
alex: ran a short repro with bw=2ms + kv_cache disabled: p95 much smoother at 210qps but throughput dropped ~8% vs previous. interesting tradeoff — cost per token still wins but throughput/latency trade.
sara: that matches hypothesis: batching delay reduction reduces tail but reduces batching efficiency. need to find sweet spot for customer SLOs.
maya: can we add a metric to eval harness to report effective batch_size_distribution and kernel_path? would help correlate.
ci-bot: note: created perf test ticket PERF-2211 to add batch_size histogram to harness output.
ops-bot: reminder: please update the canary config to fallback to fp16 if p95 > 300ms for >5m.
alex: next actions: mason runs region repro and shares logs, maya builds kernel-flag image, sara will scan autoscaler events. I'll update the dashboard with batch_size histograms once PERF-2211 lands.
mason: starting repro run now, will post results in this thread. :rocket:
maya: thanks all, this is actionable — feel free to ping me if you need help interpreting kernel traces. :+1:
